meta.purpose: Everything on this site that a reviewer should look at before trusting it. Grouped by severity, not by topic. Each row names what was expected, what was found, and where to check it.

severity_key.high: Affects whether the site can earn at all, or whether a claim on the site is currently wrong.
severity_key.medium: Affects usefulness or discoverability, not correctness.
severity_key.low: Cosmetic, administrative, or already resolved with a note.

flags.title: Every submitted path code is 9 characters; every ASIN observed on arrival is 10
flags.expected: An Amazon Standard Identification Number is a 10-character alphanumeric identifier.
flags.found: All five submitted codes (B04G1MEwY, B02NbDxp3, B00hJ57DV, B0c8moW59, B0f3GKalj) are 9 characters and contain lowercase letters. All five destinations now resolve, and they carry 10-character uppercase ASINs: B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH, B0DHZTCNR5 and B0DZFD6R9Z.
flags.impact: The intended_asin field is null for all five rather than filled with the slug. Filling it with the slug would have been an inference.
flags.reading: The submitted codes are short-link slugs rather than identifiers. The register records what arrived, and keeps the two fields separate.
flags.blocks: nothing — but it explains why one column is empty
to_check: Open each supplied link and compare the /dp/ segment to the code in the link

flags.title: Attribution to shopnow047c-20 is not confirmed by an Associates report
flags.expected: A click from this site appears in the Associates report against the supplied tag.
flags.found: The tag was not observed in any URL reached while following the supplied links. The site now appends ?tag=shopnow047c-20 to every Amazon destination, which is what Program Policies 2(b) requires, but no report has been read.
flags.impact: Links are now structurally correct. Whether they are credited is still unknown, and the site says so in its footer and on this page rather than implying success.
flags.reading: Two separate questions were being confused: does the destination carry a tag, and does the account register a click. The first is fixed. The second needs a click and a dashboard.
flags.blocks: any claim that the site can currently earn
to_check: One click from the owner's device, then Reports → Orders in the Associates dashboard

flags.title: The compliance status of the short links themselves is unresolved, not disproven
flags.expected: A statement that the supplied link form is or is not permitted.
flags.found: The links are of the form link.amazon/<code>. This build could not establish from an official source whether that is an Amazon-issued redirect that applies a tag server-side, or an untagged redirect.
flags.impact: The site does not use the short links as click destinations any more; it links to the resolved listing with the tag attached. The short link stays in the record as evidence of what was supplied.
flags.reading: Unresolved is not invalid. Nothing on the site calls these links invalid or non-compliant.

flags.title: P-04 failed three times, then resolved — and later observations disagree on which product it is
flags.expected: One short link resolves consistently to one product page.
flags.found: https://link.amazon/B0c8moW59 returned Amazon's /checkpoint/continue interstitial on three attempts in an earlier session. On 2026-11-20 it resolved on the first attempt to B0DHZTCNR5, a ThermoMaven digital meat thermometer. A parallel session later reported the same mapping. See FLG-016.
flags.impact: P-04 has a product page, a category and a tagged buy link to the destination reached here. The identity is labelled as observed-and-disputed, not settled.
flags.reading: Resolution is a record of one request, not a guarantee about the next. Neither mapping is declared correct.
flags.blocks: confident product identity for P-04 and P-05

flags.title: No price, rating, review count or stock status — by rule, not by omission
flags.expected: A shop normally shows price and rating next to each product.
flags.found: Nothing is shown, because neither permitted data path is connected. Program Policies 2(b) allows price and availability only where Amazon serves the link carrying that data, or where it arrives through Creators API or PA API.
flags.impact: Buy buttons say what they do and send the reader to Amazon, where the live figure is. No number on this site can go stale.
flags.reading: This is the one place where the site is deliberately less useful than a retailer. It is also the only version that stays true.

flags.title: No author, no byline, no first-hand testing
flags.expected: A publication normally names the person whose judgement it is.
flags.found: No byline anywhere. The site's claim is narrow and checkable: the links were opened, the listings were read, and the reasoning is shown.
flags.impact: Article structured data names the organization, not a person, because inventing an author would be a fiction.
flags.reading: An accurate anonymous voice is honest but weak. A named editor with a true biography is the cheapest credibility available, and it is logged as S-03.
flags.blocks: the site's ability to claim authority

flags.title: Every image on this site is an AI-generated illustration
flags.expected: A shop shows the product.
flags.found: Every image was generated for this build. None is a photograph of a submitted product. Each is labelled where it appears, and the policy page lists every asset.
flags.impact: A reader cannot judge the product from the picture, and the pages say so rather than implying otherwise.
flags.reading: Product imagery is licensed material with its own rules. Until a permitted source exists, illustrations are the honest option.

flags.title: Two competing editions of this site were served from one repository
flags.expected: One canonical site for search engines to index.
flags.found: A generated edition at the root and a hand-written edition under crisp/ plus duplicate root pages (products.html, questions.html, suggestions.html, guides.html, dashboard.html and others). They described the same five products with different navigation and different URLs.
flags.impact: The duplicates could compete with the canonical pages and split what little authority exists. Internal links pointed into both editions, so navigation was ambiguous.
flags.reading: Consolidated on 2026-11-20: the root build is canonical, the duplicate edition is archived under archive/legacy-2026-11-20/ with a noindex tag on every archived page, and the sitemap lists only canonical URLs. Nothing was deleted; git history and the archive both retain the other session's work.

flags.title: The previous edition's buy links carried no tag at all
flags.expected: Every Special Link includes the Associates ID as a tag parameter (Program Policies 2(b)).
flags.found: The previous build pointed at https://www.amazon.com/dp/<ASIN> with no query string, which cannot be attributed to any account. This is recorded against this repository's own earlier output, not against the operator.
flags.impact: Corrected on 2026-11-20: every Amazon destination is now built by a single function that appends ?tag=shopnow047c-20, and the checker fails the build if any Amazon product link lacks the tag.
flags.reading: This was a real defect and it was live. Publishing it here costs less than hoping nobody noticed.

flags.title: Analytics exists in the code but is switched off
flags.expected: Measurement before optimisation.
flags.found: A cookie-free client and a self-hosted collector are in the repository. Both are inert: there is no deployed endpoint and the client sends nothing by default.
flags.impact: No traffic, click or conversion data exists. The campaign ledger is empty on purpose.
flags.reading: Switching it on needs a host and a privacy statement first. Doing it in the other order would be a compliance problem for a site whose selling point is compliance.

flags.title: Amazon's own ASIN definition could not be reached from this environment
flags.expected: A first-party definition of ASIN to cite.
flags.found: Seller Central help pages return a sign-in wall. Public pages that repeat the definition are written by sellers, not by Amazon.
flags.impact: The site states the observed shape of an ASIN (ten characters) rather than citing a definition it could not read.
flags.reading: The observation is strong enough for the register's purpose: a nine-character slug is not a ten-character identifier.

flags.title: Food-safety temperatures are not restated on this site
flags.expected: A thermometer guide would normally give safe internal temperatures.
flags.found: The figures live with food-safety authorities and vary by food and cut. The guide points to the authority rather than copying numbers into a shopping page.
flags.impact: One fewer thing on the site that could be wrong, and one more click for the reader.
flags.reading: Deliberate omission with a stated reason, not a gap.

flags.title: Commission rates are blank
flags.expected: A revenue plan would start from the rate card.
flags.found: The rate card is behind an Associates sign-in and was not supplied. No forecast is offered.
flags.impact: The site makes no revenue claim anywhere.
flags.reading: Rates are per category and change; quoting one from memory would be the exact failure mode this site is built to avoid.

flags.title: The campaign ledger is empty
flags.expected: Measurement over time.
flags.found: No authorised first-party reports exist, so the ledger has columns and no rows.
flags.impact: No conversion score, no revenue forecast, no trend.
flags.reading: An empty ledger with a provenance rule is more useful than a full one with invented numbers.

flags.title: Two of the five products are thermometers, not air fryers
flags.expected: The brief describes air fryers; the register holds five links.
flags.found: P-04 resolves to a ThermoMaven digital meat thermometer and P-05 to a CHEF iQ wireless probe set. Category path on arrival for both: Home & Kitchen > Kitchen & Dining > Kitchen Utensils & Gadgets > Thermometers & Timers > Meat.
flags.impact: Thermometers are published as their own category. No guide treats them as a fifth air fryer.
flags.reading: Corrected from the earlier build, which described one thermometer and an unresolved fifth link.

flags.title: P-04 and P-05 were mapped to opposite products by two sessions, then reconciled by later observation
flags.expected: A short link maps consistently to one listing.
flags.found: This session observed P-04 (B0c8moW59) → B0DHZTCNR5 (ThermoMaven) and P-05 (B0f3GKalj) → B0DZFD6R9Z (CHEF iQ Sense). A parallel session recorded the reverse mapping on 2026-11-20. A later fetch by that session reached the same mapping recorded here, and the merged register now agrees with it. Earlier P-04 attempts still reached a checkpoint.
flags.impact: The current register is internally consistent and both product pages carry an identity note because the disagreement existed and neither observation proves intent. The intended product remains unconfirmed until the operator checks SiteStripe.
flags.reading: Agreement between sessions is corroboration, not proof. Both observations were of the same short link, so a stable redirect is plausible but the intended ASIN is still only knowable from the account.

flags.title: Archived editions contain earlier or conflicting product observations
flags.expected: One served edition, one register.
flags.found: Three editions had been published from this repository: the generated root edition, a crisp/ sub-site and a kitchen/ sub-site, plus duplicate root pages. Their registers disagree about P-04 in particular.
flags.impact: All three are archived under archive/legacy-2026-11-20/ with noindex on every page, and the published artifact is staged from the generated set only. Archived material is a record, not confirmation.
flags.reading: Old pages that still rank, or that a reader bookmarks, would otherwise contradict the current register. Archiving plus noindex removes that contradiction without destroying the history.

flags.title: Buy-button wording is a compliance judgement the site cannot make for itself
flags.expected: A shop's call to action is usually 'add to basket' or a price.
flags.found: Buttons read 'See it on Amazon' and 'Check it on Amazon', each followed by a line stating that price and rating are shown on Amazon. No figure and no implied discount.
flags.impact: Nothing on the page displays price or availability, which is what the policy constrains. The reading of the policy is the site's own.
flags.reading: Logged for owner review before any paid traffic is sent. If the wording reads as a price claim to the account owner, it is a two-line change.
flags.blocks: nothing, but it should be signed off

flags.title: The site has no Search Console property and no email list
flags.expected: A publication measures what it publishes.
flags.found: No verification token, no property, no analytics endpoint, no mailing list. RSS is the only channel that works today.
flags.impact: The next topic cannot be chosen from measured demand, only from editorial hypotheses.
flags.reading: Both are owner actions: Search Console needs the owner's Google account, and email needs a provider and a privacy statement.

flags.title: The holiday hosting photograph has no recorded origin
flags.expected: Every photograph on the site has an entry in src/data/images.json with its origin, date and generator.
flags.found: assets/img/holiday-hosting-counter.jpg is used on the index, the guides index and the holiday hosting guide. It had no images.json entry. Its contents were read directly: an unbranded countertop air fryer beside roasted vegetables and green beans, with a garland in the window.
flags.reading: Blank fields mean unknown, not safe. Until the owner records where the file came from, it is not cleared on rights or on whether it depicts a real product.
flags.impact: An entry was added with generated_on, generated_by and depicts_a_real_product left null. The guide caption calls the scene illustrative. The owner should confirm the origin or replace the photograph.
flags.blocks: a clean image audit for the holiday guide and the index card

flags.title: tools/validate.py fails on the current product schema
flags.expected: Every validator in tools/ runs clean against the current data.
flags.found: python3 tools/validate.py stops with KeyError 'supplied_path_code_length' on the current src/data/products.json. The build gate tools/check.py passes with 0 errors.
flags.reading: Only the legacy validator is affected. The publication gate that runs in CI is not. A validator that fails silently is still a gap, so it is recorded.
flags.impact: Nothing on the site depends on tools/validate.py. Either update it to the current schema or retire it and say so in the README.
flags.blocks: a clean validator is still owed; nothing else
